chunks: throw away the reins of the horses who carry on their backs the weight of your hands (i.e. sins), do not cut away from your chief (Imām) otherwise you will blame yourself for your own doings. Do not jump in the fire which is in flames in front of you; keep away from its courses and leave the middle way for it. Because, by my life, the believer will die in its flames, and others will remain safe in it.

key_terms.الازِمَّة: Reins (metaphor for authority or burden of governance)

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of throwing away the reins in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Delivered during the 'Vicissitudes of Time' (Khutbah al-Harawiyyah), this passage reflects Imam Ali’s critique of the Umayyad caliphate, urging the public to disengage from the burdens of governance to avoid the 'fire of fitnah' (civil strife). The metaphor highlights a key Shia theological insight: while political power often demands compromise that endangers the believer's integrity, the non-believer, unburdened by spiritual accountability, may survive the turmoil unscathed.
